chunks: From him, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who freed his umm walad (concubine who bore him a child) and made her manumission her dowry, then divorced her before consummating the marriage with her, he said: 'He must pay her half of her value. If she refuses, she has one day of service and he has one day of service.' He said: 'And if she has a child and he has wealth, he pays half her value on her behalf and she is freed.'

key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدٍ: Concubine who bore her master a child

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a man who frees his concubine and divorces her before consummation?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the financial settlement (mahr al-mithl or compensation) in the specific context of freeing an umm al-walad and treating manumission as her dowry, a scenario distinct from standard divorce. The Imam provides a flexible mechanism: if she accepts half her value, the debt is settled; if she refuses, it establishes a reciprocal service exchange, highlighting the balance between financial obligation and personal autonomy. In cases where he possesses wealth and she has borne a child, the full payment ensures her complete emancipation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the rights of the mother and child within the family structure.
